stem: What _____ you doing at nine o'clock last night?
explanation: "Doing" needs a form of be; the time is in the past, so the past continuous question is "What were you doing?".

stem: Have you ever _____ to Canada?
explanation: The present perfect uses have + past participle; the past participle of be is "been".

stem: She _____ in this city since 2019.
explanation: "Since" + a starting point shows a situation that continues until now, so we use the present perfect: has lived.

stem: Look at those clouds. It _____ rain.
explanation: We use "be going to" for predictions based on present evidence, such as dark clouds.

stem: We _____ our homework yet.
explanation: "Yet" is used with the present perfect: have not + past participle (finished).

stem: While we _____ TV, the lights went out.
explanation: The past continuous describes the longer action in progress; with "we" the auxiliary is "were".

stem: I _____ my keys. I can't find them anywhere.
explanation: The present perfect shows a past action with a result now (I still can't find them): have lost.

stem: The students _____ a test tomorrow afternoon.
explanation: The present continuous is used for fixed future arrangements: are having a test tomorrow.

stem: Everybody _____ the new teacher.
explanation: "Everybody" is grammatically singular, so the verb takes -s: likes.

stem: One of my classmates _____ from Japan.
explanation: The subject is "one" (singular), not "classmates", so the verb is "comes".

stem: The news _____ very good today.
explanation: "News" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb: the news is.

stem: My sister and her husband _____ in Madrid.
explanation: Two subjects joined by "and" make a plural subject: live.

stem: You _____ wear a helmet when you ride a motorbike. It's the law.
explanation: "Must" expresses strong obligation, such as a rule or law.

stem: You look tired. You _____ go to bed early tonight.
explanation: "Should" is used to give advice.

stem: Students _____ bring food into the laboratory. It is not allowed.
explanation: "Mustn't" means something is not allowed. "Don't have to" means it is not necessary.

stem: It's Saturday, so I _____ get up early.
explanation: "Don't have to" means it is not necessary.

stem: When I was a child, I _____ swim very well.
explanation: "Could" is the past of "can" for past ability.

stem: This bag is _____ as that one.
explanation: The structure as + adjective + as shows that two things are equal: as heavy as.

stem: Today is _____ than yesterday.
explanation: The comparative of "bad" is irregular: worse.

stem: She is the _____ student in our class.
explanation: The superlative of "good" is irregular: the best.

stem: The train is _____ than the bus.
explanation: One-syllable adjectives add -er: faster.

stem: There are only _____ apples left.
explanation: "A few" is used with plural countable nouns such as apples.

stem: Can I have _____ sugar in my coffee?
explanation: "A little" is used with uncountable nouns such as sugar.

stem: We need some _____ for our project.
explanation: "Information" is uncountable, so it has no plural and no a/an.

stem: I didn't buy _____ furniture for my room.
explanation: "Furniture" is uncountable; in negatives we use "much".

stem: I enjoy _____ with my friends on weekends.
explanation: "Enjoy" is followed by a gerund (-ing form): enjoy cooking.

stem: Have you finished _____ the report?
explanation: "Finish" is followed by the -ing form: finished writing.

stem: She is good at _____ problems.
explanation: After a preposition (at), use the -ing form: good at solving.

stem: _____ is good for your health.
explanation: A gerund can be the subject of a sentence: Swimming is good for your health.

stem: We decided _____ the train instead of the bus.
explanation: "Decide" is followed by to + base verb: decided to take.

stem: I went to the library _____ some books.
explanation: We use to + base verb to express purpose: to borrow.

stem: They hope _____ their studies next year.
explanation: "Hope" is followed by to + base verb: hope to finish.

stem: The cat jumped _____ the wall.
explanation: "Over" shows movement from one side of something to the other.

stem: I'm interested _____ learning Spanish.
explanation: The adjective "interested" is followed by "in".

stem: The bank is _____ the post office and the pharmacy.
explanation: "Between" is used for a position with one thing on each side.

stem: He is afraid _____ spiders.
explanation: The adjective "afraid" is followed by "of".

stem: The man _____ lives next door is a doctor.
explanation: "Who" introduces a relative clause about a person.

stem: This is the book _____ I told you about.
explanation: "Which" (or "that") introduces a relative clause about a thing.

stem: That's the café _____ we met for the first time.
explanation: "Where" introduces a relative clause about a place.

stem: Nobody helped her. She taught _____ to play the guitar.
explanation: When the subject and object are the same person, use a reflexive pronoun: she taught herself.

stem: Is this pen _____? I found it on your desk.
explanation: At the end of a clause, without a noun, use the possessive pronoun "yours".

stem: _____ is raining again today.
explanation: We use "it" as a dummy subject for weather.

stem: _____ love music. It is part of every culture.
explanation: For people in general, we use a plural noun with no article: People love music.

stem: She plays _____ piano very well.
explanation: We use "the" with musical instruments: play the piano.

stem: Our school is famous _____ its science program.
explanation: The adjective "famous" is followed by "for".

stem: Call me _____ you arrive at the airport.
explanation: "When" introduces the time something will happen.

stem: Wash your hands _____ you eat.
explanation: "Before" shows that one action happens earlier than another.

stem: Paper _____ from wood.
explanation: The passive (is made) is used when the focus is on the product, not on who makes it.

stem: Can you tell me where _____?
explanation: In indirect questions (Can you tell me...), use normal word order: where the station is.

stem: What time _____ the film start last night?
explanation: Past simple questions use "did" + base verb: What time did the film start?

stem: The museum was full of _____ paintings.
explanation: A noun (paintings) is described by an adjective: beautiful.

stem: There is a big _____ between the two cities.
explanation: After "a big" we need a noun: difference.
